conditions.label: Conductive hearing loss, unilateral, right ear, with unrestricted hearing on the contralateral side

medications.sig: Instill 5 drops in the right ear twice daily for 10 days

reports.text: Pure-tone air and bone conduction, both ears. Right: conductive hearing loss, average air-bone gap 30 dB across the speech frequencies; bone conduction thresholds within normal limits. Word recognition 96% at comfortable level. Left: hearing within normal limits, word recognition 100%. Tympanometry deferred on the right because of drainage; left type A.
reports.conclusion: Right conductive hearing loss, average air-bone gap 30 dB. Normal left ear.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery
Date of service: 01/06/2025
Referred by: primary care, for right otorrhea

History: 32-year-old woman with chronic hypertension, four months postpartum (seen by obstetrics through her pregnancy last year), with half a year of right ear drainage that is frequently malodorous, plus steadily declining hearing on the right. Background noise is the hardest part; group conversation at work is a strain. No vertigo, no tinnitus. Many ear infections in childhood with bilateral tubes, but nothing in the last twenty years.

Medications: labetalol 200 mg twice daily; prenatal vitamin daily. Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Social: daycare teacher; former smoker, about 5 pack-years, quit at 26; no alcohol.
Family: both parents hypertensive.

Examination under the microscope: Right - after suctioning of the canal, the tympanic membrane is intact but retracted, with a pearly white mass in the superior quadrant at the attic. Left - normal canal and drum. Tuning forks: conductive pattern on the right. Facial nerve intact bilaterally. Nose, oral cavity, oropharynx and neck normal.

Audiogram today: right conductive loss, average air-bone gap 30 dB, word recognition 96%; left normal.

Impression: Right attic cholesteatoma with conductive hearing loss.

Plan:
- Ofloxacin otic, 5 drops right ear twice daily for 10 days; strict water precautions.
- CT temporal bones without contrast for surgical planning.
- Surgery is the treatment. We discussed right tympanomastoidectomy, its goal of a safe dry ear, and the possibility of a later look for residual disease. She would like to proceed once the ear is drier.

Thank you for the referral.
Otolaryngology

reports.text:
Temporal bone protocol. Technique: axial thin-section images of both temporal bones without contrast, with coronal reformats.
Right: soft-tissue mass in the epitympanum with blunting of the scutum. Ossicular chain intact. Tegmen tympani and lateral semicircular canal intact. Facial nerve canal intact. The mastoid air cells are otherwise aerated. External auditory canal clear.
Left: middle ear and mastoid clear and well aerated. Ossicles normal.
Inner ear structures normal bilaterally. Visualized brain unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Right epitympanic soft-tissue mass with scutal blunting, consistent with cholesteatoma. No erosion of the ossicles, tegmen or lateral semicircular canal. Normal left temporal bone.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Pre-op evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-operative H&P for R tympanomastoidectomy 3/12 (ENT, general anesthesia, outpatient). ENT letter and CT reviewed - right attic cholesteatoma.

Feels well. Finished the ear drops, drainage much less. Climbs two flights carrying a toddler without chest pain or breathlessness. No personal or family problems with anesthesia. No bleeding history. Not pregnant; still nursing at night. Back at work.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: BP at goal, vitals otherwise normal. Airway: normal mouth opening, good dentition. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

Assessment: low-risk patient for a low-risk procedure. No testing needed beyond what ENT requires. Take labetalol with a sip of water the morning of surgery. Cleared - letter faxed to ENT surgical scheduler.

reports.text:
Specimen: right middle ear and attic, cholesteatoma matrix.
Gross: multiple fragments of tan-white flaky tissue.
Microscopic: keratinizing stratified squamous epithelium with abundant laminated keratin debris and underlying fibrous tissue. No dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Right middle ear and attic: cholesteatoma (keratinizing squamous epithelium with keratin debris). Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Operative report - right tympanomastoidectomy
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside Otolaryngology - Ambulatory Surgery Center
Date of surgery: 03/12/2025

Preoperative / postoperative diagnosis: right attic cholesteatoma.
Procedure: right canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy with tympanic membrane reconstruction (temporalis fascia).
Anesthesia: general. Facial nerve monitoring used throughout.

Findings: cholesteatoma in the attic. Ossicular chain intact and preserved. Facial nerve canal, tegmen and lateral canal intact. Matrix removed completely under the microscope.

EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same afternoon in stable condition, facial function normal.

Plan: dry ear precautions, packing to stay in place until the post-op visit in six weeks; diffusion-weighted MRI at one year to look for residual disease. Pathology to follow.
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Ear surgery went fine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just letting you know the ear surgery was last Wednesday and went well. Ear is packed and a little achy but no fever. The surgeon said it all came out. No questions, just wanted you to have the update!

documents.title: RE: Ear surgery went fine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, glad it went smoothly. Their report and the pathology just came in and confirm what they told you. Keep it dry and follow their instructions for the packing.

documents.title: Otolaryngology post-operative visit
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside Otolaryngology
Date of service: 04/23/2025

Six weeks after right canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy. Packing removed. Postauricular incision well healed. Graft intact and healing, ear dry. Facial function normal. She thinks her hearing is about where it was before surgery.

Pathology confirmed cholesteatoma.

Plan: may resume getting the ear wet in two more weeks. Non-echo-planar diffusion-weighted MRI next spring, about a year after surgery, to screen for residual disease. Sooner for drainage or pain.
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL - 33F

Interval: daughter delivered 8/2024 at 37 wk (FGR). R attic cholesteatoma removed 3/2025 (canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy), healing well per ENT; MRI planned spring 2026. Weaned from nursing in May.

Concerns today: since the winter she brings up phlegm most mornings and every cold from the toddler room seems to leave a cough for weeks. No fever, no blood, no weight concern raised. She shrugs it off as the daycare.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID; prenatal vitamin (asked about stopping; fine either way, she prefers to keep it). NKDA.
SH: former smoker, quit at 26. No alcohol.

Exam: BP at goal, vitals as charted. Weight down to 69.5 kg from 73.5 last fall, postpartum. HEENT: R ear healed postauricular incision, canal dry; L TM normal. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout, no wheeze or crackles. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin no rashes. Ext no edema.

A/P
1. Chronic HTN - controlled. Continue labetalol 200 BID. CMP today.
2. Morning phlegm / post-cold cough - likely postviral with constant exposures at work; lungs clear. Return if it changes, if blood, fever, or weight loss.
3. Cholesteatoma s/p surgery - ENT following.
4. HM - CBC, CMP, lipids. Pap/HPV due 2026. Vaccines up to date for the season; flu and COVID in the fall. PHQ-2 0.

Follow up 6 months or as needed.

documents.title: Lab results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wendy, your results are all within the normal range - blood counts, kidneys, liver, sugar and cholesterol. Nothing to do. Enjoy the summer.

documents.title: Extra labetalol before a trip
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm leaving September 8 for a two-month volunteer program overseas (rural area, back early November). Could I get enough labetalol to cover the whole time plus some extra? My pharmacy says insurance needs a vacation override.

documents.title: Vacation supply - labetalol
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Per PCP ok for 90-day supply now. Called pharmacy, vacation override requested with insurer; approved, labetalol 200 mg #180 ready 8/22. Messaged pt back.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 7 days with a full glass of water

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Consolidation in the right lower lobe. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Left lung clear. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours normal. Bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe consolidation, consistent with pneumonia.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Sick visit - cough, fever
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit (texted this morning).

S: Got home Nov 7 from two months volunteering in a rural area abroad. About 4 days ago fever up to 38.6 at home and her usual morning phlegm turned into a much heavier cough with thick yellow-green sputum through the day. No blood. Tired. No known sick contacts on the flights. No leg swelling.

Meds: labetalol 200 BID, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

O: SpO2 96% RA, other vitals as charted; weight 67.0. Mildly ill-appearing, speaking full sentences. Crackles at the right base, no wheeze; left clear. Heart regular. No calf tenderness.
CXR (read same day): right lower lobe consolidation.
CBC: WBC 13.6.

A/P: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe, fine for outpatient treatment. Doxycycline 100 mg BID x 7 days. Fluids, rest. Recheck in 2 weeks; sooner for worsening breathing, persistent fever past 72 hours on treatment, or chest pain. Travel history noted - if symptoms don't fully settle we'll think more broadly.

documents.title: Follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt day 2 of doxycycline. Fever lower overnight than before. Taking with food and water, staying upright after doses. Breathing ok, no worse. Reminded of 12/3 recheck. Will call sooner if fever persists past the weekend.

orders.reason: persistent purulent sputum with blood streaks and weight loss after right lower lobe pneumonia

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up - pneumonia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Fever broke after 3 days on doxycycline and has not come back; finished the course. But the sputum hasn't gone away: every day, thick and yellow-green, worst first thing in the morning - she fills tissues before breakfast - and it smells bad. A few times there have been streaks of blood mixed in. More tired than she'd expect, winded on stairs carrying her daughter. Looking back, the morning phlegm has been there since last winter.

Weight: 66.4 today vs 69.5 at the June physical, without trying.

O: Afebrile, SpO2 normal on RA. Coarse crackles persist at the right base. Heart regular. No nodes in the neck or axillae.

A/P
1. Persistent purulent sputum with blood streaking and weight loss after RLL pneumonia; recent two months in a high-TB-incidence region; daycare exposure. This needs a chest specialist. Pulmonology referral placed, urgent slot requested. Quantiferon today. Mask at work until we hear back on TB testing.
2. Pneumonia - fever resolved; closing as treated.
3. Weight loss - 3 kg since June, unintended. Tracking.
4. Flu and COVID given today (missed the fall while away).
5. HTN - BP fine on labetalol.

documents.title: TB blood test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your TB blood test (Quantiferon) is negative. That's reassuring, though it doesn't settle everything by itself, so the lung specialist may still want sputum samples. You can stop masking at work. Pulmonology has you for January 5.
